step1_analysis.description: A passive network consisting of an AC coupling capacitor (C1) and a termination/bias resistor (R1), with a parasitic or pad capacitance (C2). In an RF front-end, this is typically used for DC blocking and impedance matching at the input or output of an LNA or PA.

paper_reference.title: A 2.4-GHz-Band 1.8-V Operation Single-Chip Si-CMOS T/R-MMIC Front-End with a Low Insertion Loss Switch

gain_2_4GHz.description: Voltage gain (insertion loss) at the operating frequency of 2.4 GHz.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming C1=10pF and R1=50 ohms, the high-pass cutoff is 1/(2*pi*50*10pF) = 318 MHz. At 2.4 GHz, the capacitor acts nearly as a short, resulting in minimal insertion loss.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A DC blocking capacitor in a 2.4 GHz RF front-end should have negligible insertion loss at the operating frequency.

cutoff_frequency.description: The -3dB cutoff frequency of the high-pass filter.

sky130_expected.calculation: fc = 1 / (2 * pi * R1 * C1). With R1=50 ohm and C1=10pF, fc = 318 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The cutoff frequency must be well below the 2.4 GHz operating band to avoid attenuating the desired RF signal.

step3_testbench.description: AC analysis to measure the frequency response, insertion loss at 2.4 GHz, and the -3dB cutoff frequency of the passive network.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Passive RF Network

* Parameter definitions
.param val_c1=10p
.param val_c2=100f
.param val_r1=50

* DUT Instantiation
C1 n0 n1 {val_c1}
C2 n1 GND {val_c2}
R1 n0 GND {val_r1}

* Stimulus
Vin n1 GND dc 0 ac 1

* Control block
.control
  * AC Analysis from 1 MHz to 10 GHz
  ac dec 100 1Meg 10G
  
  * Calculate gain in dB
  let gain_db = vdb(n0)
  
  * Measure gain at 2.4 GHz
  meas ac gain_2_4GHz find gain_db at=2.4G
  
  * Measure -3dB cutoff frequency
  meas ac cutoff_frequency when gain_db=-3.0 fall=1
  
  * Print results
  print gain_2_4GHz
  print cutoff_frequency
  
  quit
.endc
.end
